about: Weekly 'What's new in urology' digest. Built every Monday by tools/weekly-news.mjs from PubMed and merged by pull request. Items marked pinned are hand-picked recent advances. Do not overwrite this file from an app upload.

items.title: AUA releases its 2026 guideline on LUTS attributed to BPH
items.summary: 62 statements across evaluation, medical and procedural care. Medical therapy: offer alfuzosin, silodosin or tamsulosin; a 5-ARI for prostates over 30 mL or PSA over 1.5 ng/mL; daily tadalafil 5 mg; storage drugs alone or with an α-blocker.
items.why: Doxazosin and terazosin drop out of the 'offer' list; tadalafil gains a defined first-line role.

items.title: EAU Urological Infections 2026: new fungal UTI chapter and updated biopsy prophylaxis
items.summary: A limited update adds a chapter on diagnosis and treatment of fungal urinary tract infection, revises antibiotic doses, and updates periprocedural prophylaxis for prostate biopsy, favouring the transperineal route with less antibiotic use.
items.why: Changes candiduria and prostate biopsy prophylaxis practice; see Drugs: Urinary Infections.

items.title: Gepotidacin: first new oral antibiotic class for uncomplicated UTI in about 30 years
items.summary: FDA approval (March 2025), followed by the UK MHRA, for uncomplicated UTI in females aged 12 or over weighing at least 40 kg: 1500 mg twice daily for 5 days. EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3 showed non-inferiority to nitrofurantoin.
items.why: A new option when resistance or intolerance limits standard cystitis antibiotics; GI side effects are common.

items.title: NOSTONE: hydrochlorothiazide did not prevent recurrent calcium stones
items.summary: Placebo-controlled trial of hydrochlorothiazide 12.5, 25 or 50 mg daily in recurrent calcium stone formers: no dose reduced symptomatic or radiological recurrence over about 3 years; hypokalaemia, gout and new diabetes were more common.
items.why: Challenges routine thiazide prescribing for stone prevention; select patients carefully.

items.title: TRAVERSE: testosterone therapy and cardiovascular safety
items.summary: In hypogonadal men with or at high risk of cardiovascular disease, testosterone gel was non-inferior to placebo for major adverse cardiac events, but atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury and pulmonary embolism were more frequent.
items.why: Reassures on MACE in properly diagnosed men while highlighting specific risks to counsel about.

items.title: ALTAR: methenamine hippurate vs daily antibiotics to prevent recurrent UTI
items.summary: Open-label non-inferiority trial in women with recurrent UTI: methenamine hippurate 1 g twice daily was non-inferior to low-dose daily antibiotic prophylaxis over 12 months.
items.why: Supports a non-antibiotic first choice for prophylaxis, helping antibiotic stewardship.

items.title: Which Patients with Advanced Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Benefit Most from First-line Checkpoint Inhibitor Combination Regimens: A Meta-analysis of Individual Patient Data and Aggregate Data from Randomised Trials.
items.summary: Meta-analysis of 4 first-line IO-based RCTs (n=3320) in metastatic clear-cell RCC showed no OS benefit for IMDC favourable patients (HR 0.98) and progressively larger benefit for intermediate (HR 0.78) and poor prognosis (HR 0.51); PD-L1 expression modified effect.
items.why: Helps select RCC patients most likely to profit from IO combos, especially poor-prognosis group.

items.title: Organ-preserving multimodal therapy for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma in China (DISTINCT-I): a single-arm, phase 2 trial.
items.summary: Single-arm phase 2 trial (n=20) of induction disitamab vedotin + tislelizumab followed by kidney-sparing surgery in high-risk UTUC achieved 70% 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival; grade 3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 10%, no grade 4-5 events.
items.why: Shows feasibility of kidney preservation in selected high-risk UTUC, but evidence remains limited.

items.title: Prostate and pelvic nodal stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) versus prostate-only SBRT for high-risk, localised prostate cancer (PACE-NODES): early adverse event results from an international, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
items.summary: Phase 3 open-label RCT (n=1166) in high-risk localized prostate cancer compared prostate-only SBRT (36.25 Gy) with prostate + pelvic nodal SBRT (36.25 Gy + 25 Gy). At 13.8-month median follow-up, grade ≥2 GI toxicity occurred in 21.3% vs 28.0% (absolute increase 6.7%, p=0.011).
items.why: Provides early safety data suggesting higher GI toxicity with pelvic nodal SBRT, informing treatment planning.

items.title: Urinary biomarker-guided surveillance versus standard cystoscopic surveillance for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.summary: Meta-analysis of two RCTs (n=606) in NMIBC showed biomarker-guided surveillance cut cystoscopy use by 56-75% without a significant change in overall recurrence (RR 1.04), high-grade recurrence (RR 1.03) or progression (RR 0.57), though non-inferiority was not established.
items.why: Suggests cystoscopy reduction is possible, but limited trial data prevent guideline change.

items.title: Disorders of Ejaculation: AUA/SMSNA Guideline (2027).
items.summary: 2027 AUA/SMSNA guideline update on premature and delayed ejaculation reviewed 89 studies (2020‑2024) and added statements supporting PDE5‑inhibitors, daily or on-demand clomipramine, and glans hyaluronic-acid injections, while reaffirming non-pharmacologic options.
items.why: Provides current evidence-based options for ejaculation disorders; clinicians should discuss benefits and risks with patients.

items.title: Study Rationale, Enrollment Characteristics, and Central Review of Clinical Stage: The INTACT Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: A phase III trial of 485 localized muscle-invasive bladder cancer patients evaluated clinical staging accuracy. Among 243 centrally reviewed cases, agreement between site-reported and central review was moderate, with 11.9% of cT2 cases upstaged and 35.7% of cT3-T4a cases downstaged.
items.why: Highlights staging discrepancies in muscle-invasive bladder cancer trials, impacting patient selection and trial interpretation.

items.title: Epidemiology and Modifiable Risk Factors for Benign Prostatic Enlargement and Related Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
items.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies evaluated modifiable risk factors for benign prostatic enlargement and lower urinary tract symptoms. High adiposity indices showed positive associations with BPE and moderate-to-severe LUTS. Certainty of evidence was very low.
items.why: Identifies modifiable risk factors for BPE and LUTS, though limited by very low certainty evidence.

items.title: Opioid-free anaesthesia versus opioid-based anaesthesia for laparoscopic radical prostatectomy: a prespecified analysis of a single-centre randomized controlled trial.
items.summary: A randomized trial of 57 patients undergoing laparoscopic radical prostatectomy compared opioid-free and remifentanil-based anesthesia. No significant difference in 24-hour oxycodone consumption or pain scores was found, though opioid-free anesthesia showed a lower PCA bolus ratio and smaller early creatinine rise.
items.why: Provides early, limited evidence on opioid-free anesthesia for prostatectomy, requiring confirmation in larger trials.

items.title: Phase I trial of using a prostatic urethral lift implant with stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy for men with prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia (NCT05311527).
items.summary: A phase I trial of 15 prostate cancer patients with symptomatic BPH evaluated combining prostatic urethral lift and stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy. No grade 3 or higher toxicities occurred, and mean AUASS improved from 22.1 to 14.0 at 3 months.
items.why: Offers early evidence that combining PUL with SAbR is feasible for managing obstructive symptoms in radiation-eligible prostate cancer patients.

items.title: Pelvic osteotomy in classic bladder exstrophy and cloacal exstrophy: a systematic review and qualitative evidence synthesis with separate clinical pathways.
Efficacy of HER2-targeted therapies in localized urothelial carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: Meta‑analysis of 33 studies (970 pts) of HER2‑targeted regimens, mainly disitamab vedotin, as neoadjuvant therapy for localized urothelial carcinoma. Pooled pathological complete response 48% (54% in surgery‑evaluable); bladder‑sparing clinical complete response 65%/54%; grade ≥3 toxicity ≤35%.
items.why: Limited prospective evidence; suggests promising activity but HER2 expression not predictive.

items.title: Prostate-specific antigen testing by income, age, and region: a nationwide population-based study.
items.summary: Swedish population cohort (men 40‑90, 2000‑2023) found 17% underwent at least one PSA test in 2019; testing rose with income (13% bottom vs 20% top) and age (22% at 80‑90 vs 13% at 50‑59); regional rates varied 12‑20%.
items.why: Highlights socioeconomic and age‑related overtesting, underscoring need for organized screening.

items.title: Patterns and prognostic implications of de novo distant metastasis in renal cell carcinoma: a population-based analysis of organ combinations across histologic subtypes.
items.summary: Population‑based SEER analysis of 139,373 RCC cases (19,196 with de novo metastases) showed lung (62%) as dominant site; median overall survival fell from 14 months (single organ) to 4 months (≥3 organs). Multi‑organ disease (HR 1.92) and non‑clear‑cell histology independently worsened survival.
items.why: Provides prognostic stratification by metastatic burden, aiding counseling and trial design.

items.title: Robot-assisted pyelo-ureteral reconstruction for ureteral stricture in kidney transplant recipients: functional outcomes and perioperative morbidity from a bicentric cohort.
items.summary: Retrospective bicentric series of 24 kidney‑transplant recipients undergoing robot‑assisted pyeloureteral reconstruction (median age 54). Technical feasibility 91.6%; 66.7% remained free of urinary diversion at 1 year (ITT) and 77.8% functional success among evaluable cases; morbidity acceptable, no creatinine change.
items.why: Limited evidence suggests robotic approach is feasible with reasonable success in this high‑risk population.

items.title: Clinical Prostate Score (CLIPS) stratifies quality-of-life outcomes following minimally invasive surgical therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: Prospective single‑centre cohort of 164 men undergoing minimally invasive BPH surgery (Rezum or PUL) evaluated CLIPS (Prostate volume − 3×Qmax). 68% were CLIPS‑high. Both groups improved IPSS, but only CLIPS‑high showed significant QoL gain (‑2 points) at 12 months; Qmax trends also differed.
items.why: Suggests CLIPS may help pre‑operative selection for better QoL outcomes after MIST.

items.title: Regional disparities in clinicopathological characteristics and overall survival after radical nephroureterectomy for upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional cohort study across European and Taiwanese centers.
items.summary: Multi-institutional cohort study of 2634 patients undergoing radical nephroureterectomy for upper tract urothelial carcinoma across Europe and Taiwan. Region was not independently associated with overall survival in multivariable analysis (HR 1.16, p=0.15).
items.why: Demonstrates that UTUC prognosis is driven by individual patient and tumor factors rather than geographic origin.

items.title: Kidney-sparing management of bilateral synchronous upper tract urothelial carcinoma: redefining what was once inevitable.
items.summary: Retrospective bicentric cohort of 17 patients with synchronous bilateral upper tract urothelial carcinoma treated with endoscopic kidney-sparing management. Four-year cancer-specific survival was 67% overall and 100% in low-grade disease; no patient required dialysis.
items.why: Provides early evidence that endoscopic kidney-sparing management can preserve renal function and avoid dialysis in selected bilateral UTUC.

items.title: Navigating complexity: applying machine learning to improve SWL outcome prediction.
items.summary: Retrospective multicenter analysis of 1498 patients treated with shock wave lithotripsy. Machine learning algorithms, particularly LightGBM, outperformed traditional logistic regression in predicting stone-free status (AUC 0.83) and secondary ureteroscopy need (AUC 0.92).
items.why: Highlights the potential of machine learning algorithms to improve outcome prediction following shock wave lithotripsy.

items.title: Preoperative prediction of complications after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: development and internal validation of a prediction model compared with generic risk scores.
items.summary: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 683 patients undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. A preoperative four-item model predicted 90-day complications with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.587, performing comparably to generic risk scores like ASA.
items.why: Shows that preoperative variables alone predict postoperative complications only to a limited extent, aiding resident counseling.

items.title: EPIGEN-Prostate: Identifying multi-omic markers of prostate cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand men.
items.summary: Protocol for a multicenter prospective longitudinal cohort study of patients undergoing prostate biopsy, designed to discover novel cell-free DNA methylation and multi-omic biomarkers for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer.
items.why: Outlines a biomarker discovery study aimed at improving prostate cancer detection and risk stratification; currently limited evidence.
